summary: The paper describes compiler algorithms that turn Fortran D programs, whose data layout is given by alignment and distribution directives, into SPMD message-passing node programs for MIMD distributed-memory machines. It concentrates on owner-computes partitioning, message vectorization and collective communication, and on pipelining loops whose cross-processor dependences serialize computation.
why_read: It is an early, detailed account of how a compiler derives node programs and message passing from data decomposition directives.
main_contribution: A compile-time strategy for Fortran D that partitions data and computation, generates communication sets, and applies message vectorization, collective communication and pipelining.
main_limitation: The prototype implements only message vectorization for block-distributed arrays, and the paper reports no measurements.
